_README: Registry of regulatory sources watched by scripts/reg-watch.mjs. Worldwide coverage, UAE-weighted (UAE sources first). Each source: id (stable key), name, jurisdiction, category, narrative (what it is + why watched + what it feeds in the app), url, type (html|rss|json). Edit this file to add/remove sources; the weekly Regulatory Watch workflow fingerprints each url and opens a PR when content changes. Country black/grey LIST changes are handled separately by the FATF Watchdog (scripts/fatf-watchdog.mjs); the FATF entry here watches guidance/news, not the lists.

sources.name: UAE Ministry of Economy (MoE) — DNFBP / DPMS supervisor
sources.narrative: Federal supervisor for Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions, including Dealers in Precious Metals and Stones (DPMS) and real estate. Issues DPMS guidance, goAML registration rules and the cash-transaction reporting threshold (AED 55,000). Watched so DPMS/real-estate Q&A answers and sector tools stay current.

sources.name: UAE Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) — goAML
sources.narrative: Receives Suspicious Transaction/Activity Reports via the goAML platform and issues filing guidance, formats and feedback. Watched so STR/AIF deadlines, narrative requirements and the goAML / FIU-reporting answers and the STR Drafter tool stay current.

sources.name: UAE National Committee for AML/CFT (NAMLCFTC)
sources.narrative: National coordination body owning the National Risk Assessment and AML/CFT strategy. Watched for new NRA outputs, national typologies and policy shifts that feed the EWRA, governance and typology answers/tools.

sources.name: UAE Executive Office for Control & Non-Proliferation (EOCN)
sources.narrative: Administers UAE targeted financial sanctions, the local consolidated list and freezing obligations. Watched for list updates and freeze-timeline guidance feeding the sanctions answers, the escalation/CFA logic and the risk data.

sources.name: UAE Central Bank (CBUAE) — AML/CFT
sources.narrative: Supervises licensed financial institutions and exchange houses for AML/CFT and issues circulars, the AML Standards/Guidance and examination expectations. Watched so FI-facing answers, examination-readiness and transaction-monitoring tools stay current.

sources.name: Dubai Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA)
sources.narrative: Regulates virtual-asset activity in Dubai (ex-DIFC), including AML/CFT, travel-rule and licensing rulebooks. Watched so VASP / virtual-asset answers and the VARA compliance tool stay current.

sources.name: Dubai Gold & Jewellery Group / DMCC (sector)
sources.narrative: UAE gold and jewellery sector bodies issuing codes of practice and responsible-sourcing expectations (DMCC Rules for Risk-Based Due Diligence). Watched so sector-specific gold/jewellery answers and tools reflect current sector guidance.

sources.name: FATF — guidance, recommendations & news
sources.narrative: The global AML/CFT standard-setter. This entry watches FATF publications, guidance and Recommendation revisions (NOT the black/grey lists, which the FATF Watchdog handles). Feeds most Q&A citations and tool reference lists.

sources.name: Wolfsberg Group
sources.narrative: Bank-industry body issuing principles and questionnaires (correspondent banking, CDD, CBDDQ). Watched so correspondent-banking and CDD answers/tools reflect the latest Wolfsberg standards.

sources.name: Responsible Minerals Initiative (RMI)
sources.narrative: Runs the Responsible Minerals Assurance Process (RMAP) smelter audits and the Conflict Minerals Reporting Template (CMRT). Watched so the RMI / minerals answers reflect current audit protocols and templates.

sources.name: LBMA — Responsible Sourcing
sources.narrative: Sets the Responsible Gold Guidance (RGG) and Good Delivery refiner standards. Watched so LBMA answers and gold-sourcing logic reflect current RGG steps and refiner rules.

sources.name: OECD — Responsible Mineral Supply Chains (CAHRA)
sources.narrative: Owns the Due Diligence Guidance for Responsible Supply Chains of Minerals from Conflict-Affected and High-Risk Areas (the 5-step framework) and MNE Guidelines. Watched so OECD answers and the high-risk-country / ASM risk floor reflect current guidance and Annex II shifts.

sources.name: US OFAC — Recent Actions
sources.narrative: US Treasury sanctions authority. Watched for designations/de-listings and 50%-rule guidance feeding the sanctions answers and the escalation/CFA logic (secondary-sanctions exposure for UAE gold trade).

sources.name: UN Security Council — Consolidated List
sources.narrative: The UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, implemented in the UAE without delay. Watched for designations under 1267/1988/1718 etc. feeding the sanctions/TF/PF answers and freeze logic.

sources.name: EU — Financial Sanctions
sources.narrative: EU consolidated financial-sanctions list and ownership-and-control guidance. Watched so the EU 'ownership and control' answers and blocking-statute (Reg 2271/96) content stay current.

sources.name: UK OFSI — Consolidated List of Targets
sources.narrative: UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation consolidated list and guidance. Watched for UK designations relevant to correspondent and trade-finance exposure.

sources.name: Egmont Group of FIUs
sources.narrative: Global network of Financial Intelligence Units governing FIU-to-FIU information exchange. Watched so the Egmont information-request and cross-border cooperation answers/tools stay current.

sources.name: Basel AML Index
sources.narrative: Basel Institute composite country ML/TF risk scoring. Watched so the country-risk weighting in the EWRA and customer risk-rating logic can be recalibrated when scores are republished.

sources.name: UNODC — Money Laundering & Organised Crime
sources.narrative: UN Office on Drugs and Crime publishes money-laundering, organised-crime and predicate-offence typologies, the Vienna/Palermo convention guidance and the GPML programme outputs. Watched so the typology, predicate-offence and international-cooperation answers reflect current UN crime research and methodologies.

sources.name: EU — High-Risk Third Countries (AML/CFT)
sources.narrative: The European Commission list of third countries with strategic AML/CFT deficiencies (Delegated Regulation), which triggers mandatory EDD on relationships involving listed jurisdictions. Watched so the high-risk-jurisdiction EDD answers and country-risk weighting in the EWRA stay aligned with EU additions/removals.

sources.name: Responsible Jewellery Council (RJC)
sources.narrative: Sets the RJC Code of Practices and Chain-of-Custody standard for the jewellery and watch supply chain (responsible sourcing, KYC, conflict-sensitive due diligence). Watched so the gold/jewellery sector answers and responsible-sourcing tools reflect current RJC certification requirements.

sources.name: PROBE u.ae AML portal
sources.narrative: Temporary probe candidate for the MoE AML page on the official UAE government portal. Branch-only; removed before merge. Exists to verify fetchability from a GitHub runner.

sources.name: PROBE u.ae AML national strategy
sources.narrative: Temporary probe candidate for the CBUAE AML/CFT rulebook section. Branch-only; removed before merge. Exists to verify fetchability from a GitHub runner.

sources.name: PROBE OECD minerals due diligence publication
sources.narrative: Temporary probe candidate for OECD mineral supply chain guidance on the new oecd.org site. Branch-only; removed before merge. Exists to verify fetchability from a GitHub runner.
